machine.note: author workstation; CI runs Ubuntu. No container engine, Python runtime or CI runner is used by this lab.

model.basis: Minutes for a learner who has finished the covered topic pages for that day. The lab is repair-and-complete: the compose draft ships commented with named defects, the Dockerfile and pipeline are teammate drafts, and main.py's docstring lists the three rules its call breaks. Reading time uses the frozen page estimator rates (200 words per minute, 15 code lines per minute) for the README and the architecture brief; editing time is judged from the edit distance between each draft and the private solutions (compose about 8 changed lines after uncommenting, Dockerfile 3 changed lines, main.py about 10 changed lines, ci.yml about 12 changed lines, 30 worksheet choices plus 6 why sentences).

phases.phase: setup and first run (outside the required core)
S38 2 repair the reviews services in Compose
S38 5 architecture and data review (22 choices, 4 why sentences) and a test pass
S39 7 images and delivery review (8 choices, 2 why sentences)

requiredCoreBounds.S38: about 39 minutes inside S38's 85-minute guided-lab block
requiredCoreBounds.S39: about 16 minutes inside S39's 85-minute guided-lab block, which also holds the module check
requiredCoreBounds.outsideCore: the one-time setup (about 3 minutes) is outside the required core

model.wrongFirstRetry: a failing test costs about 1 minute to read the message, make the one named repair and rerun; the drafts localize each failure
model.worstRequiredBasis: typical 55 plus about 5 minutes of extra retries and brief rereading reaches the 60-minute bound the README names as the pause-and-self-study point
model.fit: Each day's share occupies that day's existing frozen-calendar Lab-template guided-lab block (85 minutes) and adds no required time elsewhere.

learnerCommands.note: node --test --test-reporter=tap finishes in well under a second on the starter and on both private solutions

notObserved: No human learner has been timed. The phase minutes above are a model, not an observation.
